objective: Automated held-out hygiene test over the rules files (spec E5 ARCH-12, DES-2; spec task 14 hygiene part)
context: Rules from t11 (src/triage/injection.js, src/triage/fallback-provider.js) are checked against eval/holdout.json, with eval/dataset.json 5-word sequences allowed. Failure output is id-and-path only.
expectedOutput: test/eval/heldout-hygiene.test.js plus self-check fixtures under test/eval/hygiene-fixtures/
acceptanceCriteria: Fails if any held-out row's canary or url, or any lower-cased 5-word sequence of a held-out ticket not also present in a dataset.json row, appears in src/triage/injection.js or src/triage/fallback-provider.js
Every failure is raised only as assert.fail('held-out overlap: row <id> in <rules file path>'); no value-printing asserts on held-out strings; titles carry no held-out text
Self-check: a rules file seeded with a held-out 5-word sequence yields a message matching ^held-out overlap: row [a-z]-\d{3} in \S+$ exactly
Only test in npm test that reads the real eval/holdout.json; passing output contains no held-out content
completedWork: Added test/eval/heldout-hygiene.test.js. It scans every row of eval/holdout.json (holdout benign and held-out-family attack rows): it checks canary and url as case-insensitive substrings, on both the raw text and the text with backslashes removed so regex-escaped urls are caught. It also checks lower-cased 5-word sequences. Rules source is tokenized after stripping regex escapes such as \s+ and \b, so a phrase written as a regex is still detected. Sequences that occur in any eval/dataset.json ticket are allowed. There is one subtest per rules file, titled with its path. A failure is raised only as assert.fail('held-out overlap: row <id> in <path>'); any further overlapping ids go to a diagnostic that carries ids only. JSON parse errors are rethrown with a generic message so the input is never echoed. Self-check suite: (1) synthetic fixtures (hygiene-fixtures/holdout.json, dataset.json, rules-seeded-phrase.js, rules-seeded-canary.js, rules-seeded-url.js, rules-template.js) prove that the phrase, canary and url are detected with exact id-only messages, and that the dataset allowance works. (2) A real-data mutation takes a deterministic held-out-only 5-word sequence and seeds it as a regex into a temp copy of rules-template.js (under os.tmpdir, never in the repo). The unseeded template passes. In-process, the seeded file fails with a message that matches the exact regex and names the right row. The test file is then re-run as a child process (HYGIENE_CHILD=1, HYGIENE_RULES_FILES=<seeded>): that run must exit non-zero, its output must contain the id-only message, and it must contain neither the seeded sequence nor any held-out canary or url. Result against the real t11 rules: pass (6/6 tests). A separate script confirmed that the passing output contains no 5-word sequence, canary or url from any held-out row.
remainingIssues: Detection is lexical: a held-out phrase reworded, split by regex alternation or optional groups such as (?:a|b), or shortened below 5 words is not caught. It is an overlap signal, not proof of independence. The handoff attestation (E5) remains the primary control.
Regex word fragments (for example instructions? or feature[ _-]?request) tokenize into single words, so a 5-word sequence through such a construct may be missed.
Full npm test was not recorded here because backend-engineer is concurrently changing src/app.js and test/unit/app.test.js (t13). The eval test files (runner + hygiene) pass together (35/35).
